idiom_name: by lazy delegate for the one-shot check, lateinit / use-named gate functions
implementation_notes: The stdlib supplies the deferral: by lazy(LazyThreadSafetyMode.SYNCHRONIZED) computes the value - and therefore runs the check - only on first access, PUBLICATION lets threads compute independently and NONE is the single-threaded fast path, while lateinit var defers assignment and fails at first read with UninitializedPropertyAccessException. The rules themselves stay ordinary functions (require/check inside a validateForPublish() member), because Kotlin has no annotation-driven validation in the standard library, so the lazy delegate plus a use-named function is the whole structure. A validator class hierarchy is still justified when rules are shared across targets or come from configuration.
pitfalls: lazy(LazyThreadSafetyMode.NONE) is not thread-safe: the property may be seen uninitialised from another thread, and SYNCHRONIZED adds locking plus a volatile read to every subsequent access.

lateinit cannot be used for primitives and gives no visibility guarantee across threads, so a deferred check built on it can surface UninitializedPropertyAccessException instead of a validation message.
Each delegated property allocates a delegate object, so a lazy validation on a hot path or per element of a large collection costs an allocation and a synchronised check.
